content: The condition and characteristic of a vulgar person is that he never looks for either help or harm from himself, but only from externals.
author: Epictetus
story:
Born into slavery in Hierapolis and physically crippled by a brutal master in imperial Rome, Epictetus acquired his freedom after Nero's death and founded a renowned philosophical academy in Nicopolis. Having experienced genuine subjugation, he founded his philosophy on the inviolable inner freedom of the human will: chains may bind the body, but no tyrant can conquer the faculty of choice.

In formulating this reflection, Epictetus stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of external blame. For Epictetus, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
